issues.legal_issue: A person may have a place of residence in an area that later became part of Pakistan even if the person also had a place of residence in India, and residence does not require exclusive or actual residence immediately before partition.
material_facts: The family had a business branch at Harunabad, and evidence accepted by the Tribunal indicated that Sukh Lal stayed there from time to time while also staying at Fazilka.
After disturbances at Harunabad, Sukh Lal migrated to India and later resided there.
The High Court treated actual residence at Harunabad immediately before partition as necessary, but the Supreme Court found that test erroneous.
issues.conclusion: A place of residence is a place where a person has a dwelling house, which need not be permanent or exclusive; a person may have more than one place of residence. Sukh Lal established that Harunabad was one of his places of residence and that he was displaced from it, so he qualified as a displaced debtor. The other appellants did not establish a place of residence there.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(10) and 2(6) of the Displaced Persons (Debts Adjustment) Act, 1951, a person may qualify where the person had a place of residence in an area now forming part of Pakistan and was displaced from that residence for a specified reason, even if the person also had a residence in India. Residence means a dwelling place and may be non-permanent and non-exclusive; purely temporary sojourn does not suffice. No earlier cases are relied upon.

rule.if: displaced_debtor_adjustment_proceeding and qualifying_debt_claimed and pakistani_dwelling_place and qualifying_residence_displacement and later_resided_in_india

predicates.displaced_debtor_adjustment_proceeding: The matter concerns a claim for adjustment of a debt on the basis that the debtor is displaced.
predicates.qualifying_debt_claimed: A creditor claims a debt from the person that falls within the class of debts covered by the adjustment claim.
predicates.pakistani_dwelling_place: The person had a dwelling place in an area that later formed part of Pakistan, whether or not the person also had a dwelling place in India.
predicates.qualifying_residence_displacement: The person left or was displaced from that dwelling place because of the division of the dominions, civil disturbances, or fear of such disturbances.
predicates.later_resided_in_india: The person subsequently resided in India.

issues.definition: When a debt-adjustment claim involves a qualifying debt, a Pakistani dwelling place, displacement from that dwelling place for a qualifying reason, and subsequent residence in India, the claimant qualifies as a displaced debtor even if the claimant also had a dwelling place in India.

issues.legal_issue: The closure or loss of a business in an affected area does not itself displace the business owner or establish the owner’s status as a displaced person.
material_facts: A branch of the family business at Harunabad was closed after riots, and goods pledged to the bank were looted.
Some family members were shown to have resided at Harunabad, but there was no evidence that Karam Chand or Prabh Dayal had a place of residence there.

The appellants argued that the joint family should be treated as displaced because its business at Harunabad had closed; the joint-family residence contention had not been raised in the lower courts, and there was no evidence that the four members’ residence there was the residence of the joint family.
issues.conclusion: Displacement under the Act concerns the person, not the person’s business. Closing a business does not confer displaced status. The Court did not decide whether a Hindu joint family could itself be a person for this purpose; Karam Chand and Prabh Dayal remained unqualified on the evidence, and their liability was to be determined under the applicable apportionment provisions.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(10) of the Displaced Persons (Debts Adjustment) Act, 1951, concerns a person who has left or been displaced from a place of residence for a specified reason. A person’s status arises from the person’s leaving or displacement, not from the closure of a business the person carried on. Section 22 governs apportionment of joint debts. No earlier cases are relied upon.

predicates.displaced_debtor_adjustment_proceeding: The matter concerns a claim for debt adjustment based on displaced-person status.
predicates.business_closed_due_to_disturbance: A business carried on by the claimant was closed because of disturbances or related events.
predicates.personal_residence_displacement_establis: Evidence establishes that the claimant left or was displaced from a place of residence for a qualifying reason.

issues.definition: In a displaced-debtor proceeding, closure of a business due to disturbances, without established displacement of the claimant from a place of residence, does not establish displaced status.
